newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end slightly higher, mirroring Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end slightly higher, mirroring Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed slightly higher on Thursday after drifting in parallel with activity on Wall Street.
"I think the market is very much on hold while waiting for Q4 earnings reports. Volume was sparse, and the bourse ended up because of a late turnaround in the Dow," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX ended up 1.67 points, or 0.05 percent, at 3,654.66. Volume .TV.MX, was 109.3 million shares, of which cross trades accounted for about a third.
Traders noted that share prices zigzagged throughout the session, generally mirroring the Dow industrials.
A Iusacel source told Reuters that institutional investors appeared to be buying the stock on speculation that official approval was forthcoming for a management takeover by Bell Atlantic.
Traders noted that Iusacel had been inactive since January 28 and had lagged behind advances by its ADR, which closed flat at 9-1/4.
Most heavily traded gainer was financial group Banacci A shares, up 26 centavos to 14.76 after a hefty cross trade by the group's own brokerage.
